questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design robust, scalable upgrade workflows in multi-tenant CNF platforms, with strict isolation and observable rollouts.

## Key Concepts
- Canary deployments in Kubernetes
- Per-tenant isolation (Namespaces, NetworkPolicies)
- SLO-driven rollbacks
- Health checks, PDBs, and chaos testing for resilience

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-canary
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
      tenant: tenant-a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: tenant-a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: myregistry/cnf-gateway:canary
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 1m }
      - setWeight: 50
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate rollback correctness under node failure using chaos testing?
- What metrics and alerting would you use to enforce the 0-downtime guarantee?

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: tenantegress
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: TenantEgressConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package tenantegress

      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.kind == "EgressRule"
        tenant := input.review.object.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.tenants[tenant].allowlist
        dest := input.review.object.spec.destination
        not dest in allowed
        msg := sprintf("destination %v not allowed for tenant %v", [dest, tenant])
      }
```
